entries.effect: a localized string is an NSString whose text is chosen when it is asked: the dictionary given is copied, its keys are offered to NSBundle's matcher with the preferred languages (AppleLanguages) alone, then with en_US appended, and the first answer that is a key is the text; with no answer, the dictionary's first enumerated key. It reads as that text (length and characters), copies to a localized string with the same dictionary, mutable-copies to a mutable string, and decodes as a plain NSString; an empty dictionary answers nil and reads as empty; the host crashes on a nil dictionary, which the port answers as empty and does not reproduce
entries.source: the macOS CoreSpotlight framework of the host (tests/backports/host/corespotlight-localized, 2,240 lines over 35 preference lists (12 held out) and 61 key sets (19 held out), identical after addresses are replaced, with a planted control that the same comparison tells apart); the rendered header of CSSearchableItemAttributeSet.h from the macOS SDK for the declarations
